sentences.text: 1. Heard Mr. M. Nath, learned Senior counsel assisted by Mr. A. Bhattacharjee, learned counsel for the petitioner.

Also heard Ms. R. Borah, learned Standing counsel, NHIDCL for the respondent Nos.
1 to 3; Mr.J. Handique, learned State counsel for the respondent Nos. 4 to 6, Mr. B. Choudhury,
learned Standing counsel, APDCL for the respondent No.7 and Ms. M. Das, learned Standing counsel, PWD for the respondent No.8.

2. The grievance of the petitioner is that though the land acquisition compensation for acquisition of land has been paid to the petitioner by the National Highways Authority, however, the costs of building and zirat have not been paid.

Thereafter, on the request of the petitioner, the competent authority has made an assessment, but till date, no compensation has been paid to the petitioner on the basis of such assessment made by the authority.

3. Ms. Borah, learned Standing counsel, NHIDCL referring to Section 3G(2), 3H(3), 3H(4), 3H(7) of the National Highways (NH) Act, 1956 and Section 3H(1), 3H(2), contends that the process of determination is over and admittedly the payment has already been made in terms of Section 3H(2)
of the NH Act, 1956 and the competent authority shall have no jurisdiction to entertain any claim thereafter and the proper authority to decide the claim shall be the arbitrator in terms of Section 3G(5) of the NH Act, 1956.
Therefore, this writ petition may not be entertained.
4. This matter needs further consideration.
5. Issue notice, returnable after 4 (four) weeks.
Page No.# 4/4 6.
As the learned counsels duly represented the respondents, no formal notice need to be issued to the aforesaid respondents.
7. Extra copies of this writ petition in requisite numbers be served upon the aforesaid counsels for the respondents within a period of five days from today.
8. On the returnable date, the respondents shall be ready with their instructions or shall file their affidavits.
9. List accordingly.
